# NCBI BLAST+ 2.17.0 official Linux build (ncbi-blast-2.17.0+-x64-linux; sha256 of its bin/makeblastdb c1ffdcf6f15d1d8d75377cc9f37afa42bc9fa06678903bad77c2641e60778fce):
# `prlimit --fsize=<limit> -- makeblastdb -in in.fa -dbtype <prot|nucl> -parse_seqids -blastdb_version 4 [-hash_index | -max_file_sz 2000B] -out o/db`
# with SIGXFSZ ignored (a full disk: every output file that passes <limit> bytes fails), the input of tests/makeblastdb_failed_index.rs;
# host: the Owner's WSL2 machine (Ubuntu), under the oracle lock, 2026-11-21. Kinds: p4 (3 proteins), n4 (6 nucleotide sequences of 300 bases),
# m6 (130 proteins in 6 volumes). Version 5 databases cannot be frozen with prlimit: the LMDB file fails first, in both programs.
# Line per field: `case <kind> <limit>`, `rc`, `err`/`out` (stderr and stdout, \n \t \\ escaped, the output directory <D>, the time <T> and
# the duration <S> masked, the date string that failed to parse in `Time string '...'` as <DATE>), `files` (the number of files of the output
# directory, then `name:size` of its index, alias and metadata files, `*` for the size of a file that holds the build's date), `pjs` (the
# metadata file, its last-updated masked). rc -11 is NCBI's SIGSEGV, which LOSAT refuses (exit status 1). The rows of exit status 255 cut the
# date inside "Nov" (limit 24) and after "Nov " (limit 25): a cut inside the digits of the day or the time gives another message
# depending on the day and the hour, which the date table (index_dates.tsv) covers.
# Frozen again under a fixed clock (2026-11-21, 2026-11-05 and later days 2026-02-09 .. 2027-01-01 checked): the shim faketime.c (kept with the
# line's records, library-20261031/PUB/O/O1e/datefix/) is LD_PRELOADed on every process of the run (time, gettimeofday and clock_gettime of
# CLOCK_REALTIME return FAKE_TIME), TZ=UTC, the same binary and command as above, same host, 2026-11-21. At 2026-11-21 05:07 (day of two digits,
# hour of one digit: the class of the original run) the 18 rows below are byte-identical to the original run, which validates the shim. At
# 2026-11-05 05:07 (day of one digit) 15 of the 18 cases are identical and m6 95, 100 and 111 differ (the cut lands one byte later in the date of
# the alias file or of a volume's index): their rows of that class follow the others, with the tag `d1` after the limit on the `case` line. An
# untagged row holds for every day unless a `d1` row of the same case exists; the test picks the class by the length of the date LOSAT writes.
# The same outcomes came out at 2026-02-09, 2026-03-09, 2027-01-01 (one digit) and 2026-03-10, 2026-05-31, 2026-07-10, 2026-09-21, 2026-12-31 (two
# digits): the month's name has 3 letters and the year 4 digits, so only the digits of the day and of the hour change the date's length.
